transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-30 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Miguel Torres (Redwood CSM); Lisa Wu, Tom Reynolds, Nina Patel, Rajesh Kumar, Maya Singh (AstraHealth)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining on a holiday week, appreciate it. we wanted to keep this short - main goal is finalize rollout plan for the pilot cutover, canary and monitoring. 
[00:18] Lisa Wu: thanks Alex. quick context, we've been running the pilot for two weeks, the model is serving in our staging cluster with Redwood hosted endpoint and we did some inline caching. overall latencies look ok but we saw a couple of spikes last thursday during batch job runs.
[00:36] Priya Nair: got it, yeah i saw those traces. I think the spikes correlate with the nightly ETL pushing a big prefix - prefix caching gets cold and the KV cache warms slowly. we can tune batching and TTLs, also consider prefix prewarming before cutover.
[00:55] Tom Reynolds: yeah the SRE note - those spikes pushed 95p from 120ms to 640ms for about three minutes, triggered our paging rule. want to avoid that in prod.
[01:12] Alex Chen: ok so two approaches: a) adjust batch config + prewarm cache b) schedule cutover outside heavy ETL windows. also for canary we can limit traffic and run a short A/B where new model variant is compared to baseline. what's your preferred roll forward?
[01:32] Lisa Wu: we prefer canary + gradual ramp. start at 2% for 2 hours, move to 10% for 24 hours, then 30% for 48 hours if metrics are green.
[01:45] Nina Patel: from security, we need to validate KMS integration and audit logs in the private deployment path - even though this pilot is hosted, our compliance requires the same encryption controls. Miguel, can you share Redwood's KMS notes?
[02:02] Miguel Torres: yes, i'll share the SOC2 and KMS integration doc; for hosted we do envelope encryption and you can bring your own keys via KMS, and we keep audit trails for admin actions. i'll upload that after the call.
[02:18] Rajesh Kumar: on success metrics, product wants pass rate >= 98% for bot classification, token latency 95p < 200ms, and no functional regressions detected by our evaluation harness.
[02:32] Priya Nair: note on functional regressions - we can wire Redwood Optimize eval hooks into your regression suite to fail the rollout if BLEU-like or embedding-sim diffs cross threshold. we can set automatic rollback.
[02:48] Maya Singh: how does rollback look operationally? is it automated or manual?
[02:54] Priya Nair: we can do both. typical pattern: automated fallback to baseline model if latency or error rate breaches thresholds for X minutes. also manual rollback via console if there are semantic issues. runbook should have both triggers and actions.
[03:12] Tom Reynolds: what about A/B testing? we want to compare outputs side-by-side, not just traffic split. can we shadow traffic?
[03:20] Alex Chen: yes, Redwood supports shadowing and side-by-side logging for diff analysis. for pilot we'll propose canary + shadowing at 10% to collect outputs without user impact, then analyze.
[03:32] Lisa Wu: on monitoring, we need alerts for latency, 5xx rates, and a model-quality signal - like embedding drift or classification accuracy drop. can Redwood emit model-quality metrics to our Datadog?
[03:45] Priya Nair: absolutely. we'll emit CPU/GPU utilization, token throughput, latency p50/p95/p99, 5xx rates, and a model-quality webhook you can route to Datadog. we'll share standard dashboards.
[03:58] Nina Patel: we also need audit logs for prompt ingestion and data retention policies - do you redact PII by default?
[04:06] Miguel Torres: by default we don't alter customer payloads, but we offer configurable data redaction and retention policies. for Private deployments we can enable stricter controls. i'll include redaction notes in the doc.
[04:20] Alex Chen: ok circling back to canary specifics: Lisa suggested ramp plan. who owns the runbook? Priya to author, Tom/SRE to review, Lisa to sign off. Priya - can you outline rollback triggers?
[04:35] Priya Nair: yes. proposed triggers: 1) latency p95 > 300ms for >5 minutes, 2) 5xx rate >0.5% sustained for 10 minutes, 3) model-quality regression > 2% absolute drop on evaluation set. if triggered, automated fallback to baseline for traffic portion; full rollback manual after investigation. i'll draft with exact thresholds and play-by-play.
[04:58] Tom Reynolds: add an alerting escalation: pager at first threshold, slack channel for eng, and post-mortem requirement if rollback occurs.
[05:07] Alex Chen: good. A/B vs canary: we plan canary for traffic ramp plus shadowing to collect A/B outputs. we should also plan for a quick quantization fallback if we see memory pressure - any concerns?
[05:22] Lisa Wu: our infra team is fine with quantized model variants as long as we validate output quality. product needs to see no regression in high priority intents.
[05:33] Rajesh Kumar: can we run a short A/B with quantized variant on 5% shadow traffic to check quality delta?
[05:40] Priya Nair: yes, we can. that'll be part of the pre-go checklist.
[05:46] Maya Singh: timeline - we want go-live in the first week of July if all checks pass. can the team meet that?
[05:54] Alex Chen: timeline seems tight but feasible. key dependencies: runbook completed, pricing/contract addendum agreed, and SRE sign-off on alerts.
[06:05] Miguel Torres: i'll put SOC2 and KMS docs in shared drive today, and CSM will attempt to expedite contract paperwork.
[06:13] Lisa Wu: for traffic shift, we want a dry-run cutover this Friday to validate the routing and prewarm caches - it's internal traffic only. is Redwood able to do a dry-run?
[06:23] Priya Nair: yes, we can coordinate a dry-run. we'll prewarm prefixes and run the dry-run during low load; we'll monitor closely.
[06:30] Tom Reynolds: we need to ensure runbook includes steps for manual scaling adjustments and how to add GPU capacity in dedicated pool if needed.
[06:40] Priya Nair: noted - include autoscaling play, how to trigger burst capacity, and cost implications. Alex, can you include a cost estimate for dedicated vs hosted during the pilot?
[06:50] Alex Chen: i'll send detailed pricing options. quick ballpark: hosted for pilot is lower up-front but dedicated gives predictable latency if you need strict SLOs. i'll include delta per 100k tokens.
[07:04] Nina Patel: one last security ask - we need RBAC mappings and SSO/SAML integration verified for the Redwood console.
[07:12] Miguel Torres: yes, SSO is supported and we have RBAC roles for model deployment and runbook actions. i'll attach the integration steps.
[07:22] Alex Chen: great. recap - Priya will draft runbook and monitoring playbook, Miguel provides compliance docs, Alex sends pricing/contract, Lisa confirms canary traffic %, Tom provides alert thresholds. we'll meet to review runbook on 2026-07-07. anything else?
[07:37] Lisa Wu: sounds good. thanks all.
[07:40] Alex Chen: thanks, we will follow up - end.

Notes on transcript quality: a few transcription errors (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cash", "Redwood Dedicated" rendered as "Redwood Dedicate" in some auto-captions). There was occasional overlap and filler words preserved to keep realism.
